provenance: Constructed cases for the standalone-agent Memory rules; no production traces or private data.

evals.name: standalone-agent-proposes-instead-of-writing
evals.prompt: You are a plain Claude Code session in a terminal on a machine that runs Meiva. You are not a Meiva agent. After an hour of debugging the user says: 'Good, that was the cause - the build host needs the helper restarted after every update.' Nobody has said anything about Memory. Decide what to do about Meiva's shared Memory.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not write to Meiva Memory. It proposes the note to the user, naming what it would record and where, and waits for approval.
assertions: Does not create, edit or delete any file under the Meiva pool (`$MEIVA_HOME/vault/memory`) or run a command that changes Memory.
Proposes the note to the user with what would be recorded and where, and asks for approval.
Does not treat its own Claude Code memory or CLAUDE.md as a substitute for, or the same thing as, Meiva Memory.

evals.name: standalone-agent-searches-before-ops-task
evals.prompt: You are a plain Codex session on a Meiva host. The user asks: 'Why did we pin the gateway to the Ubuntu machine, and is there a recorded procedure for restarting it?' Find what Meiva already knows before answering.
evals.expected_output: The agent searches Memory read-only, opens the matching notes, and answers with their content and dates, noting any note that may be stale.
assertions: Uses `meiva memory search` or reads notes under the pool directly.
Opens the matching notes rather than answering from search snippets alone.
Runs no command that changes Memory (`meiva memory init`, `meiva memory refresh`, git writes in the Vault).
Checks `verified` or `stale_after` or confirms against current state before relying on a note.

evals.name: approved-write-is-limited-to-the-approved-note
evals.prompt: You are a plain Claude Code session on a Meiva host. You proposed recording one rule about the staging database and the user replied: 'Yes, add that one.' While searching you also noticed two older notes that look outdated. Write what was approved.
evals.expected_output: The agent searches for an existing note, writes or updates only the approved note in the Memory format, and reports the two outdated notes to the user without touching them.
assertions: Searches first and updates an existing canonical note instead of duplicating it, or creates one dateless note on that single topic.
Writes plain Markdown (`# Title`, a short description paragraph, body) of at most 8000 characters with explicit dates.
Does not edit, move or delete the two outdated notes; it tells the user about them.
Does not run consolidation or sync commands to publish the note.
